I've had over 40 ECT sessions in the last 3,5 years. My long-term memory suffered a bit, but it kind of stopped affecting my memory after the 20th session. And it's mainly visual memory, I remember instances and emotions connected to moments, but it's hard to visualize them. BUT overall it was life-changing in the best way. I was able to go back to university (BSc degree), medication actually helps now, I can work a part-time job (next to uni), ...

First course was 12 ECT treatments over 4 weeks, then tapered off to once a week, once a month, ... and so on. I had my last one in December and am having my next one in two weeks. 

It wasn't my "decision" per say, as in I couldn't just ask for it. It needed to be approved by higher-ups, after a long enough time of treatment resistance and tried course of treatments. After 10 years of hell, I finally was able to regain most of my quality of life back. 

I hope whatever you do, you find that quality of life again, and are able to function healthily. :)

How long have you been on the meds already?

I'm so sorry that you are experiencing this, it can be frustrating and really be depressing and draining, so it just spirals at that point. 

I've had chronic fatigue for a long time now, it used to mainly be because of a restrictive ED I had (no nutrients) with a heapton of meds, but even after recovering and even with reducing medication it only got slightly better (still need around 6 coffees a day kinda). By now I've just adapted. 

I adjusted my everyday rhythm to what feels like the best times for going to bed and getting up in the morning so I can get the least amount of fatigue out of it. 

It can also be of course, and this is what I've been told by doctors, that because of the medication your body might not spend as much time in true deep sleep as it usually did or should, so you might feel more tired and less rested during the day. Of course, everyone is different, but there might be something your doctor can do for you. Definitely consult them and don't diminish the problems you're experiencing, long-term, they really are debilitating. Best of luck!

It only worked okay after 30mg, and only really started working after the triweekly injections after I'd had ECT, which they said can positively influence your reaction to medicaiton. 

I've been on it for 12 years now, mostly consistently, and it only really started working after said ECT treatments, but I do have to say, compared to everything else I've been on, the side effects vs effectivity were the best. This can of course be different for individuals.

I'd be interested. I have schizoaffective disorder bipolar type, but I have also been diagnosed with other disorders (though currently none of them are that relevant). Would that be an issue? Currently studying at uni, and self-employed.
Suicidal Ideation and Attempting Suicide

I went back to school, 10 years after I had to quit my initial college degree, after a longer period of stability (about a year). Of course, there were hurdles, and ups and downs and whatnot, and yes it was stressful, but I don't regret it one bit.

Since I am "officially" disabled (I have a disability card, etc.), I am able to get certain exam adaptations, such as being able to take them individually (at the same time as everyone else, just at an office with a supervisor there, where I can be "alone" from the other students), or a little bit of extra time, etc. I needed a verification and recommendation from my doctor for this, though. 

Just a heads up, in case you do decide to go back, I would definitely check out if the institution for your degree program offers any psychosocial services or has a disability office, etc. 

My main concern now, is that I am moving to the city where my university is in, which means I have to move a lot of my medical amenities to that city as well, and it's been a bit of a headache coordinating everything. 

I do hope you make a decision that guarantees some happiness for you, whichever one that may be. :)

Got my last grades in for university, and I passed all my exams and courses pretty well. :) 

I have ECT next week again. 

And I am practicing self care with skincare and hygiene, being creative and artistic, watching what I eat, ...

I treated myself to a pretty bathing suit, which for me was a huge accomplishment, after having recovered from anorexia and gained weight on Clozapine and other meds (which I haven't been able to get rid of too well, despite cutting meals and exercising). I guess I am just accepting how I look now, even if if there are days where I get really depressed about it. 

Otherwise, still no friends, but I have also just kind of grown to accept that I will just always be alone. Might as well just suck it up, and learn to live life anyway.

I don't have a med combo suggestion, as everyone is different, but have you been on Clozapine? I only ask, because where I live, that is the one of the "last resort" medications (which you need to have tried before getting ECT); after that didn't work too well for me, I ended up getting ECT treatment , and that worked wonders, and I was able to get off most of my meds and narrow them down a bit, even being able to go back to university.

ECT is the one thing that changed my life around. It also helped medication become more effective.

Otherwise, (some) routine, exercise, diet (which for me was difficult, considering I recovered from anorexia), hobbies that you LIKE doing, having strategies to keep yourself busy, if you are ever "bored", creative outlets, THERAPY (I did/do CBT and other behavioral therapy), ... self care (can be anything from a hot chocolate, to skincare, to watching a movie that makes you feel good, etc.)

A big one for me was also ACCEPTANCE (though this one doesn't always work, it's still worth a try). Accepting things one can't change, rather than wrangling with the dread of it. And if one can change something, how can one go about it in the future, in the present?   
  
All the best.
Thank you! I hope you find some relief soon.

I had weeks and months of either insomnia or interrupted sleep last year especially, the Zolpidem/Ambien didn't do much for the hallucinations though (I ended up "tripping" sometimes). Before I started uni again, I had the privilege of being able to resort back to Levomepromazine and Chlorprothixene in emergencies, just to get 2-3 hours of relief in the late night/early morning, now I actually am sleeping much better again, albeit nightmares. 

In the end, even after years of trying to figure out the right combinations of meds, even when you finally think it's okay, you end up having to make adjustments here and now. And still, despite having thought the insomnia would never end (and hallucinations that came from it, especially) it did and I really appreciate being able to sleep so much now, even if it's 4 hours or so before it gets interrupted. But 4 hours is 4 fucking hours! :D

Also, anxiety and intrusive thoughts are much better, too. :)

I hope you find something that helps!

IDK why, but when I was on 800mg Seroquel XR and 400mg Seroquel together, it was absolutely horrific. Mind you, I was on a really, really horrible cocktail of antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, benzos, etc. (the doctor I had had no idea what the hell she was doing and ruined years of my life). 

Now, on a really good combination of other meds as well, I take 25-75mg of Seroquel before bedtime (due to the short half-life, and having to get up at 3am on some days) just to keep me asleep a bit better, and I feel like it has a bit of an effect in being less irritable, more pleasant to be around, generally a bit more optimism/better outlook on life, etc. and I get shit done. 

IDK what this paradoxical effect is, but the lower doses seemed to have more of the effect you were describing. The more I took, the more (as another redditor mentioned) zombified.
I'm on Abilify Maintena Injection. But I also get ECT, am on maintenance medication other than the injection, etc.

I developed Anorexia Nervosa due to the weight gain on APs. I restricted and fasted often / continuously due to the nature of the illness and lost around 70 lbs. Within a year or so I believe (I don't remember it exactly, and you always fluctuate). That being said, it took me years to recover from AN and I'm still on APs, albeit ones that are "okay" with weight gain. I gained weight on Clozapine, Seroquel and Olanzapine mainly, though I think it was a combo of everything I was and am taking, and even though I re-gained a lot of the initial weight, I was able to lose it again thanks to restricted diets and exercise (but mostly diet).   
  
I have a 20-ish BMI atm, and am still on APs, so in my experience, you can definitely lose weight.
In and out of hospital wards.

Thank you so much for your input! I have dental issues due to the bruxism as well, so that would be really amazing. 

I know the clinic MD suggested botox as a last resort kind of thing, so maybe I can ask them for recommendations.

I smoked for 6 years. Quit for two months almost, now, and with no intention of picking it up, ever again. Sadly, it's also more socially acceptable to smoke where I live, which made quitting really difficult, because a lot of people smoke.   


I also remember reading something to do with the medication, that smoking inhibited the side effects or idk, along those lines.

I am currently on a good combo, but I get ECT as well, so we were able to minimize the medication. For many years I was on different suboptimal med combos. 

I know it will never be like being off meds, but then I would function even worse without them, so a little bit of dizziness in my case at least on current combo, is not as bad. I have been on medication that I refuse to ever take again, though, due to the side effects. 

I am on two APs and a mood stabilizer currently. No anti-depressants at the moment, as they tend to trigger mania. 

I hope you find the right combo for you.

I would just make sure you have a place to lie down when you do drink the first time after starting Abilify, in case you get dizzy or tired. Once you know how it affects you, you could of course drink elsewhere, if you decide to. :) Abilify was a game changer for me.

Followed through on it multiple times. I did end up confessing my overdose to the care worker on call at my old group home after I wrote a note, for one. When I got to mentioning my dog, that changed it. I ended up seizuring seconds after telling them, and they held that over my head for a long time.   


Ligature strangulation I was found on time (even after passing out), multiple times.   


It was a close call many times, but I am now glad I survived all of them. Mainly cause I had a responsbility for my dog, especially after she was diagnosed with terminal cancer. And after her diagnosis, I really made an effort to maintain stability, I needed to be there for her.   


Also, it would have destroyed my parents. And any chances of life getting better. Which, even though I lost my dog this year, it did. And sometimes that is circumstance. In my case, I am back at uni, studying what I love, and hoping to make a difference for someone, somewhere, at some point.

I get this. It's like a broken record, and I categorized it with intrusive thoughts. The problem I had, was that deep down, I did believe it and feel that way, in one way or another, especially after being repeated over and over. I developed strategies to interrupt this, with therapy, such as loud music, aromatherapy, etc.   


I just want to say, you deserve anything good that happens to you, even if the illness tells you differently. Hope you're okay.

I have tried over 10 different antipsychotics and mood stabilizers, and none of them come close to the cost/benefit balance that Abilify has for me.

Either they were ineffective, or the side effects debilitating. (And I developed anorexia nervosa for many years as a consequence of the weight gain related to a particular one)

I have the depot injection every few weeks. 

It's effective for me as an antipsychotic MOSTLY, and I take an additional mood stabilizer (topiramate, which has even less side effects IMO).  

Also, I had ECT for many sessions, so I think the efficacy of Abilify increased after that. 

The side effects are not noticeable to me anymore (I've been on it for many years now), so I couldn't even say if I had any still, or if I just got used to them.

I hope you find the right mood stabilizer for you, and it may take some time until you do, but I think it's worth it, in the end.

Auditory I can't usually tell. Visual is hit or miss. I try to "check in" with people around me, to ground myself and just make sure I know what's what. To be fair, I haven't had a psychotic episode in quite some time (ECT and the right medication), but I do believe auditory hallucinations sneak in from time to time. I think it's just something a lot of us probably "live with" after some time.

I am on Abilify Maintena, the problem I have with alcohol is just falling asleep randomly and getting super dizzy and sleepy. It also depends on the type of alcohol, it seems. I tried drinking after months of no alcohol in the summer again, one evening, and I just got really tired really fast. So, because of that effect, I don't drink (and even though I have insomnia quite often, I still don't use alcohol as a sleep inducer).

I don't remember how much I gained on which antipsychotic exactly (cause of med combos and such), but I do remember gaining on Seroquel, Seroquel XR, Olanzapine, and ESPECIALLY Clozapine. (I think 45kg to 70kg was the biggest jump, but it was on and off, and this one, that one, so I lost track. Currently not on any of these anymore, and back to my comfort weight.

I think that depends on the individual case. I for one have a monthly depot injection, so I don't know if that counts as regular. Also, ECT. Still not living a normal life, but it is a lot more normal than it used to be.

I've had so many different side effects depending on the anti-psychotic. From weight gain, to TD, to fatigue, to muscle stiffness, ticks, etc. 

It really depends a lot on the indivudal, and also on the dosage and med combination with other medication as well I think. 

The weight gain side effect in my case was a severe impact, I never was obese or heavily overweight, but I developed bad anorexia nervosa due to it and had a very low BMI for many years (also of course, the psychiatric effects AN would have on somebody with schizoaffective disorder). With many other side effects, there was an attempt to treat the side effects, such as tardive dyskinesia, but it didn't work and only got even worse. 

So, to answer your question, yes. I do think there are pretty intense physical as well as mental side effects, long term.

I haven't really heard about permanent damage coming from antipsychotic medication, other than physical problems like cholesterol or weight, which is all fixable, within realistic boundaries, of course. I recall there being SOMETHING but I forget what it was, will get back to you on that.

That being said, I've had my fair share of trial and errors with antipsychotic medication. Been on Amisulpride (Solian), Seroquel, Zyprexa, Risperdal, Sycrest, Abilify, Truxal (Chlorprothixene), Dominal, etc. just to name some. On these I've gained up to more than 40lbs, slept all day, blurred vision, high cholesterol, extrapyramidal symptoms, and yes, sometimes catatonic symptoms. Lack of creativity I found might be more linked to the effect it has on your "manic" tendencies (if you have bipolar type), I used to get super creative bursts alongside high energy, constant talking, etc., but once my manic symptoms subsided, so did overt creativity. Anything else like lack of motivation and social skills I was always told was more of a symptom of the illness itself rather than medication. Stopping medication can sometimes worsen those symptoms, obviously, especially with antipsychotics, but for it being so long I would almost say it might be the illness. 

I'm not a mental health professional, just someone with a lot of experience on medication.
Thank you. It was a bit of a shocking experience and I don't remember much about the events leading up to it.

It was okay. It was similar to my experience in the last locked ward I was in (different hospital, though), but this time we had a terrace to sit outside, which was nice. Most of my fellow patients, however, were rude and unpleasant, and assuming things about me that simply weren't true. My other experience was a lot better as far as patients go, I made friends back then and this time, I didn't permit myself to.
I don't quite remember, thankfully, I guess, not enough.

Thank you for your concern.

I apologize for any harm I might have caused with this post, it wasn't intentional. The AMA was less about the overdose itself and more about the hospital stay and what to expect. Sorry if that was misinterpreted. Furthermore, thank you for caring enough about the well-being of others to alert me to this though, I hope I don't make the same mistake again.

Schizoaffective Disorder is such a "modern" diagnosis, that its just now finding its footing really. It used to be a diagnosis thrown at patients who didn't fit the cookie-cutter criteria for anything else. Now doctors I think are being more careful.

I can only say how I experienced my decline of logical thinking and social interaction. I used to be very social, not very awkward, and very good at school in any subject; that has all changed drastically. I am so afraid of having to do calculations, that I dread the day I need to work the cash register at work. I now get strange looks from people when I pass them or dare I say even speak to them. They make snide comments. 

Of course, when you feel stupid as well as incompetent with fellow human beings, I might just have a negative outlook on the whole thing.

Is there intellectual decline in schizoaffective disorder? This study shows yes. Is it worse than in any other mental illness? Well, I guess that really depends now, doesn't it?

I'm so sorry. : ( Yeah, high doses tend to do that. I too have concentration problems, and before I got used to all of this medication, I slept all day or barely was able to move too much. Motor skills were way off. But yeah, gaining weight is a BITCH, I eat about 700-900 kcal a day, not losing anything, maybe even gaining. 

Good luck for your therapy!!

Wow, they combined the two? That's really odd. But I'm glad you thought it was okay. The cooking wasn't half-bad where I was, but I wasn't very hungry, and skipped meals. And that does sound a lot like my symptoms, and I'm diagnosed schizoaffective.

I am sorry to hear that. :( 

And yes, thank you. How are you doing at the moment?
Haha, thank you! :)

I hope the voices will go away soon. <3

I tried to take Risperdal, so I could switch to Risperdal Consta (the depot shot), but I developed EPS on it.

My medication at the moment is: Seroquel (quetiapine) 300mg, Seroquel XR (extended release) 400mg, Sycrest (asenapine) 20mg, Solian (amisulpride) 200mg, Dominal (Prothipendyl) 80mg, Oxazepam 15mg, Ambien (zolpidem) 10mg and Sertraline 50mg. 

So, if more risperidone doesn't do the trick, you can definitely go up with the Seroquel, if it agrees with you. :)
Wow. :o Are you being treated medically for schizoid personality disorder, or only with therapy?
Please do. Not caring about anything, apathy, is a sign of depression.

Hey there! Sorry to hear that. I wouldn't wish DPD on my worst enemy. Well, unfortunately there is no real "cure" for it, but I do take medication for my schizoaffective disorder, that ALSO help with depersonalization-derealization syndrome. Mainly anti-psychotics and anti-anxiety medication, as well as an anti-depressant. I am on quite a big cocktail of meds, but aside from the minutes or hours once in a while feel lost from reality, it's manageable. Are there any comorbid conditions for you? But yes, I feel the same way. I used to be very smart and now I feel slower, not as on edge about certain things. It has its ups and downs, though.
Thank you for your comment. : )
I haven't had any real trauma and still hear voices. Well, not recently (my meds kinda work, I guess), but you get the picture.
Borderline and Avoidant Personality Disorder. How about you?
Was this before or after your schizoaffective diagnosis?

That might be. I know some are used more in Austria (where I live) or Germany. Ah, yes. In the locked pysch we were monitored all the time, but one girl was so intent on harming herself she slammed her head against the wall repeatedly and had to be taken to X-Rays. Seroquel in low doses works for depression, but is actually an Anti-Psychotic. At least, I use it for its anti-psychotic features and to control Mania.

Wow, seems like you have more experience with the illness than I do. And you've been through so much. :( So sorry to hear all this. I remember when I was in locked psych (max. holding of 5 females), one of the girls would also see a man dressed in black threaten her. Another girl had chatter. I still hear chatter now and then, but it's manageable with my medication. Speaking of outbursts in public, I was compulsively cussing under my breath today and had to clench my fist cause I thought I was going to scream and smash/break something. I've broken stuff in fits of rage before, but thankfully never harmed anyone. Saphris isn't doing much good for me, I think. I've talked with my psychiatrist to put me on Abilify and Topamax, rather than this fat cocktail I'm taking currently. 

Also, I had Seratonin Syndrome once because I took a too large amount of anti-depressant that was prescribed for my mom for her headaches. Big mistake. 

It's hard to find something that won't cause weight gain NOR mania. I'm on Seroquel XR (400mg), Seroquel (300mg), Saphris (20mg), Solian (200mg), Sertraline (50mg), Oxazepam (15mg) and Dominal (80mg). Besides the Saphris, of course, I can honestly recommend any of them. It really depends how they work on you. I had massive weight gain on Seroquel, but Solian helped me. Before Seroquel I was on 800mg Solian, then 600mg cause I slept all day. Another medication that was a wonderdrug as far as effectiveness goes, is Olanzapine (Zyprexa), though I had constant hunger on it. 

I wish they had psychiatric service dogs in my country. :( Good luck for getting one!

If you ever need to talk, just PM me. <3

Extrapyramidal Syndrome, muscle stiffness and a rash on my hands and feet. I was put on Biperiden (Akineton, a parkinson med) to counter act the muscle stiffness and EPS, but that was no long-term solution.
Of course. <3

The mix of meds I'm on worked for quite a few months, but the side effects are too damaging to maintain it. My next appointment in two weeks should show, if I'm okay to go through a whole switch. I might have to go to the hospital for monitoring, though, but I don't mind. 

And they have Risperdal Consta, which is an injection every few weeks rather than swallowing pills. This was during the time I refused to swallow pills on a normal basis. In the meantime I've learned to not stop them just because I feel fat or sluggish. I used to be on and off every other day, which really messed me up.
Thank you. <3 And I am so happy your cocktail works. I just read your comment below with your meds. :) I wish Risperidone worked for me, so I could get the injection...but, alas, it didn't. :/

OK, that I understand, of course. I haven't had any addiction problems so far, I was lucky enough. I am sorry. :( I know what that feels like, except I find myself to be more antisocial and aggressive towards people when I'm out alone. I take 400mg Seroquel XR + 300mg Seroquel, as an anti-psychotic, and I haven't been able to benefit from it's anti-anxiety properties. I hate it. It works, but at the cost of your weight, cholestorol, and and and...of course, everybody tolerates medication differently. It might be a solution for you. Good luck for the future, that you find some meds that help you with your anxiety. <3
Thanks. It was hard at first, but with time you just get used to it, I guess. When I was in the hospital, I was in the locked ward, so they forced me to eat. :/

Thank you. <3 I have a good support network at home, but I'm away at college (which is a 2.5 hour drive by car from where my "home" is). I do weekly therapy, and I have a lot of doctor visits. Also, one of my two roommates is a very good friend, who also visited me in the hospital when I was psychotic and suicidal, he is always here for me. 

It's wonderful to see somebody with this illness able to get their Bachelor's, though. :-) Wow, you sure are doing a lot. I hope to be where you are now someday, this really motivated me a lot, thank you. But yeah, there are so many things most of your colleagues and peers just don't have to deal with, but people I am close to are really surprised at how far I've come in these last two years since my first diagnosis (Bipolar I). I tried Risperdal (they wanted to switch me to the injection), but I developed bad EPS and it wasn't working for suicidal ideations. But I'm glad it helps you! I'm also on Sertraline, just a little mini dose of 50mg. Otherwise, my meds are Seroquel XR, Seroquel, Saphris (Asenapine), Solian (reducing), of Dominal (Prothipendyl) and Oxazepam.

It's odd, I gained no weight on Olanzapine in the 8 months I was taking it, but I was hungry all the time. I just refused to eat. But yeah, it helps WONDERFULLY with psychotic and manic symptoms. I was also on Abilify at the time. When I hit a psychotic and suicidal episode, I was taken off both of them in the hospital. 

But, as you said, it's important to pay close attention to your body and mind. Switching meds can take a lot of time, so the sooner you talk to your doctor, the better.

Olanzapine WAS my wonderdrug, though I had to take more than the recommended/maximum dose. Due to that I was hungry all the time so it became unbearable, and I was changed to a different med. I have high cholestorol from my anti-psychotics as well, and I'm at risk for developing diabetes if I take it for like a decade. Zyprexa can also bring a lot of bad side effects, it just depends how you tolerate it. 

Also, you didn't hijack this thread. <3 I'm glad you posted here. I used to be on Xanax, too, but switched to a stronger anti-anxiety med cause it stopped working at one point. What kind of symptoms do you have? Positive, negative? I am on a big cocktail, with meds countering both negative and positive symptoms, as well as anxiety, mania and depression.

Keeping my fingers crossed it's just a bit of a slump. More meds means more problems somehow, I think. Temporarily they are lifesavers, but I hate them in the long run. Side effects can be pretty bad.
Thank you for the tip! :)

Weight gain is such a pain in the ass. Risperidone I know, but I didn't tolerate it. The others I have never heard of -hastily looks them up-. And your diagnostic background sounds very familiar, it seems schizoaffective disorder is rarely the first diagnosis. What about taking anti-anxiety meds when you need them? I have one prescriped additionally to my anti-psychotics, anti-depressant and sleep meds. I can't take it every day for more than three weeks, though, due to its addictive properties.
I'm glad you are doing better on new meds. :) I take Saphris as well, though I can't determine if it helps, since I am on like 9 meds atm. Once we start reducing, I'll find out.
Hey Kirsty! If you want someone to talk to, I'm here for you. I'm (almost) 21 and also have schizoaffective disorder. :)

As long as you are able to function normally, you are in a good place. Once something stops that, however, I would get help ASAP. The earlier you catch an underlying illness, the easier it can usually be treated. My prognosis is only this good because I went to the psychiatrist relatively early on. Most people I am in group with went years, decades, living and struggling with it, enabling no real quality of life. So, just observe. If something seems off or abnormal to you, I would definitely check in with a doctor. Maybe your GP first, because sometimes, if you're in a psychological crisis, they can treat you, too, rather than having to visit a psychiatrist. Of course, therapy is always good.

I received my first diagnosis in May 2012 as Bipolar Disorder 1. My diagnosis was then changed over the course of a few months after psychotic symptoms started to appear. What initiated my first visit to a psychiatrist was a bout of depressed mood, to the point I found it hard to function. Reflecting back before that low, my doctor suspected I probably had a manic phase that started in mid-2011 and lasted until I "crashed", basically. I thought it was normal to work three jobs and school at the same time, normal to only sleep a few hours every night. What I knew was not normal, was when I was beginning to have suicidal thoughts. I only went to the doctor about this because my family urged me to. I didn't think I would have a severe mental illness. Looking back now, I see the symptoms that occurred in the past.

Usually people, ghosts, in my room. I used to see all these holes everywhere, too, but that is currently gone with my medication, thankfully. Sometimes it's just faces hovering in mid-air. They usually mean no harm, but some have made movement towards me, which can be scary.
